f: Step 1: 11 t - 8844 = 11 (t - 804). Step 2: compression by 11 with shift right by 804. Check: the common wrong answer is 8844, the unfactored constant.

q: The system y(t) = 107 x(t) + 71 is:
o: Time-varying but linear
Memoryless, therefore linear
Linear: it is a straight-line graph
Nonlinear: zero input gives output 71, violating the zero-in zero-out rule
h: Test x = 0 first; a linear system must answer 0.
f: Step 1: with x(t) = 0 the output is 71, not 0. Step 2: superposition fails, so the system is nonlinear (affine). Check: the term 107 x(t) alone would be linear; the offset 71 breaks it.

q: For x[n] = {203, 201} and h[n] = {439, 468}, the sum of all output samples (sum of y[n]) is:
h: Sum of a convolution = (sum of x) x (sum of h).
f: Step 1: sum of x = 404, sum of h = 907. Step 2: product = 366428. Check: direct convolution gives y = {89117, 183243, 94068}, summing to 366428.

q: H(s) has denominator s^2 + (-59) s + (858), i.e. poles at s = 33 and s = 26. For the causal system:
o: Anticausal and stable for every ROC
Stable because the poles are real
Causal but unstable: a pole is not in the left-half plane
Unstable only if the zeros are in the right-half plane
h: Causal + stable needs every pole strictly in the left-half plane.
f: Step 1: poles are 33 and 26. Step 2: at least one pole is not negative, so the causal ROC excludes part or all of the jw axis: not BIBO stable. Check: zeros do not decide stability.

q: A causal discrete-time LTI system has a single pole at z = 2.225. It is:
o: Unstable only for complex poles
Causal but unstable: pole on or outside the unit circle
Stable because the ROC is outside the pole
Stable whenever the pole is real
h: Causal + stable needs every pole strictly inside |z| = 1.
f: Step 1: |pole| = 2.225 is not below 1. Step 2: the causal ROC outside the pole excludes the unit circle: unstable (compare the accumulator pole at z = 1).

q: A filter has peak magnitude response 908. At its 3-dB frequency the magnitude is: (spaced-repetition variant 5695)
h: 3-dB means half power, so magnitude scales by 1/sqrt(2).
f: Step 1: |H| at 3-dB = 908 / sqrt(2). Step 2: = 642.053. Check: (642.053)^2 is approximately half of 908^2 = 824464, confirming half power.

q: A signal band-limited to fm = 1841.7 kHz has Nyquist rate:
h: Nyquist rate = 2 fm.
f: Step 1: rate = 2 x 1841.7 kHz. Step 2: = 3683.4 kHz minimum sampling rate. Check: sampling exactly at this rate is phase-sensitive, so real systems add margin and an anti-alias filter.

q: A noiseless B = 1441 kHz channel must carry 17292 kbps by the Nyquist formula. The number of signal levels L needed is:
h: Rate = 2B log2(L); solve for L.
f: Step 1: log2(L) = 17292 / (2 x 1441) = 6. Step 2: L = 2^6 = 64. Check: L is a power of two, as a whole number of bits per symbol requires.

q: An AM carrier has Pc = 238 W and modulation index mu = 0.86. Total transmitted power is:
h: Ptot = Pc (1 + mu^2 / 2).
f: Step 1: mu^2/2 = 0.3698. Step 2: Ptot = 238 x 1.3698 = 326.01 W. Check: sideband efficiency rises with mu and peaks at 33 percent when mu = 1, motivating DSB-SC and SSB.

q: A continuous-time state model has dominant eigenvalue lambda = -320 (real). The free response is:
o: Stable because the eigenvalue is real
Stable: dominant eigenvalue has negative real part (CT)
Stable for every input matrix B
Decided by the C matrix alone
h: CT state stability follows eigenvalue real parts, as with s-plane poles.
f: Step 1: the mode behaves as e^(-320 t). Step 2: it decays, so the model is stable. Check: this is the same left-half-plane rule as Module 5, stated for A.

q: A discrete-time sinusoid cos(pi 266/78 n) has fundamental period N0 =
h: Need Omega0 N / (2 pi) to be an integer, with Omega0 = pi m/k in lowest terms.
f: Step 1: Omega0/(2 pi) = 133/78 after reduction. Step 2: smallest N making Omega0 N a multiple of 2 pi is N = 78. Check: Omega0 x 78 / pi = 266, an even integer multiple relationship holds: True.

q: For x[n] = (0.876)^n u[n], the value x[4] is:
h: Raise alpha to the power n; u[n] = 1 for n at least 0.
f: Step 1: x[4] = (0.876)^4. Step 2: value = 0.5889. Check: |alpha| = 0.876 is below 1, so the sequence decays.

q: A memoryless system is y = x^2 (sample values). Feeding the single sample x = 289 + 236 gives output:
h: Apply the rule to the summed input, do not sum separate outputs.
f: Step 1: summed input = 525. Step 2: y = (525)^2 = 275625. Check: separate outputs would sum to 139217, which differs, proving nonlinearity.

q: For x(t) = u(t) and h(t) = u(t) in a continuous-time LTI system, y(323) is: (spaced-repetition variant 5696)
h: The output is the ramp r(t) = t u(t).
f: Step 1: y(t) = integral from 0 to t of 1 dt = t for t at least 0. Step 2: y(323) = 323. Check: differentiating y returns u(t), the step response relationship h = ds/dt holds.

q: X(s) = 543 / (s (s + 307)). The final value x(infinity) is:
h: Final-value theorem: limit of s X(s) as s tends to 0.
f: Step 1: s X(s) = 543/(s + 307). Step 2: at s = 0 this is 543/307 = 1.7687. Check: the remaining pole at -307 is in the left-half plane, so the theorem applies.

q: y[n] - 0.2596 y[n - 1] = x[n]. The pole of H(z) is at z =
h: Transform: Y(z) (1 - a z^-1) = X(z); the pole solves 1 - a z^-1 = 0.
f: Step 1: H(z) = 1 / (1 - 0.2596 z^-1). Step 2: denominator zero when z = 0.2596. Check: this matches the pair a^n u[n] with a = 0.2596.

q: A sawtooth-type Fourier series has harmonic coefficients b_k = 2A/(k pi). For A = 379 and k = 25, b_k is:
h: Substitute A and k into 2A/(k pi).
f: Step 1: b_k = 2 x 379 / (25 pi). Step 2: = 9.6512 (4 decimal places). Check: coefficients fall as 1/k, slower than a triangle wave (1/k^2) but faster than the constant spectrum of an impulse train.

q: A DFT uses N = 2048 samples taken at fs = 1032192 Hz. The bin spacing is:
h: Spacing = fs / N.
f: Step 1: spacing = 1032192 / 2048. Step 2: = 504 Hz between bins X[k] and X[k+1]. Check: N bins x 504 Hz spans the full 1032192 Hz sampling rate.

q: Output power is 92.99 times the input power. The gain in decibels is:
h: dB = 10 log10(P2/P1) for powers (20 log10 is for voltages).
f: Step 1: ratio = 92.99. Step 2: 10 log10(92.99) = 19.68 dB. Check: ratio 0.5 gives about -3 dB and ratio 10 gives +10 dB; sign follows gain versus loss.

q: A 128-ary modulation runs at 8445 baud. Its bit rate is:
h: Bit rate = baud x log2(L).
f: Step 1: bits per symbol = log2(128) = 7. Step 2: bit rate = 8445 x 7 = 59115 bps. Check: denser constellations raise rate at fixed baud but need higher SNR for the same error rate.

q: For A = [[0, 1], [-638, -218]] (companion form), det(A) is:
h: det [[p, q],[r, s]] = p s - q r.
f: Step 1: det = (0)(-218) - (1)(-638). Step 2: = 638. Check: det(A) equals the product of eigenvalues, here the constant term of s^2 + 218 s + 638.

q: For x(t) = 339 cos(2 pi 331 t) (1 ohm reference), the average power P is:
h: P = A^2 / 2 for any sinusoid, independent of frequency.
f: Step 1: identify amplitude A = 339. Step 2: P = A^2/2 = 114921/2 = 57460.5. Check: average of cos^2 over a period is 1/2, and frequency 331 Hz does not change the average.

q: Evaluate the integral over all t of (t^2 + 603) delta(t - (-190)) dt:
h: Sifting: the impulse samples the bracket at t = t0.
f: Step 1: sifting property: integral of x(t) delta(t - t0) dt = x(t0). Step 2: x(-190) = -190^2 + 603 = 36703. Check: everything away from t = -190 is multiplied by zero.

q: The system y[n] = x[n] + x[n - 866] is classified as: (spaced-repetition variant 5697)
o: With memory and noncausal
Memoryless and noncausal
Memoryless and causal
With memory, causal, linear and time-invariant
h: It uses the present sample and a past sample only.
f: Step 1: x[n - 866] is a past sample, so the system has memory. Step 2: no future samples appear, so it is causal. Step 3: it is a fixed linear combination with constant coefficients, hence linear and time-invariant.

q: Convolving x[n] = {89, 183} with h[n] = {549, 674} (both starting at n = 0), the value y[1] is:
X(s) = 1 / ((s + 48)(s + 106)) with causal ROC. In x(t), the coefficient multiplying e^(-48 t) is:
h: Cover-up: set s = -a in 1/(s + b).
f: Step 1: partial fractions: A/(s+48) + B/(s+106) with A = 1/(106 - 48) = 0.0172. Step 2: x(t) = (0.0172 e^(-48 t) - 0.0172 e^(-106 t)) u(t). Check: x(0+) = 0, matching the initial-value behaviour of this strictly proper X(s).

q: x[n] = (0.8034)^n u[n]. The sample x[3] is:
h: Cube the base; u[3] = 1.
f: Step 1: x[3] = (0.8034)^3. Step 2: = 0.5186. Check: |a| = 0.8034 is below 1, so the ROC |z| above 0.8034 includes the unit circle: decaying and stable.

q: An odd square wave of amplitude 497 has sine harmonics (4A/(k pi)) sin(k w0 t) for odd k. The amplitude of the k = 3 harmonic is:
h: Substitute k into 4A/(k pi).
f: Step 1: amplitude = 4 x 497 / (3 pi). Step 2: = 210.9334 (4 decimal places). Check: it falls as 1/k, so higher harmonics weaken - the origin of Gibbs ripple concentration near jumps.

q: A 495 Hz tone is sampled at fs = 787 Hz. It aliases to:
h: Fold: alias = |f - k fs| for the integer k giving a result in [0, fs/2].
f: Step 1: Nyquist needs fs at least 990 Hz, so 787 Hz undersamples. Step 2: alias = |495 - 1 x 787| = 292 Hz. Check: 292 lies in [0, 393], the representable baseband.

q: Bandwidth B = 433 kHz and SNR = 22 dB. The Shannon capacity is approximately (bps):
h: C = B log2(1 + SNR), with SNR converted from dB first.
f: Step 1: SNR linear = 10^(22/10) = 158.489. Step 2: C = 433000 x log2(1 + 158.489) which is about 3168398 bps. Check: Shannon is an upper bound; a practical rate must stay below it, then Nyquist sets the levels.

q: AM with modulating bandwidth BWm = 214.7 kHz has total transmission bandwidth:
h: AM keeps both sidebands: BWt = 2 x BWm.
f: Step 1: sidebands sit at fc +/- up to 214.7 kHz. Step 2: BWt = 2 x 214.7 = 429.4 kHz. Check: SSB would need only 214.7 kHz, at the cost of sharper filtering.

q: A state matrix A has characteristic polynomial lambda^2 + (65) lambda + (64). Its eigenvalues (the system poles) are:

1 and 64
-1 and -1
h: Factor the quadratic: (lambda - r1)(lambda - r2).
f: Step 1: lambda^2 + (65) lambda + (64) = (lambda - (-1))(lambda - (-64)). Step 2: eigenvalues are -1 and -64. Check: sum of roots = -65, product = 64, matching trace and determinant relations.

q: Total energy of x(t) = e^(-370 t) u(t) (1 ohm reference) is: (spaced-repetition variant 5698)
